items.title: 4.7.1 Strategy for the identification of the limiting reactant

source_refs.note: Topic 4.7.1, printed pages 86-87; Sample Problems 4.17 and 4.18, with Quick Check 4.9 as the self-check. The print's NH3 mass and N2 molar mass slips in Sample 4.17 are noted.

items: Calculate the number of moles from the given amounts of the reactants.
Find the number of moles of product that each would give, from the balanced equation.
The reactant that produces the least amount of product is the limiting reactant; the other is the excess reactant.

blocks.title: Did you know
blocks.text: Fire is a combustion reaction in which fuel and oxygen combine, usually at high temperature, to form water and carbon dioxide; once started it is self-supporting. Smothering quenches a fire by reducing the available oxygen below the level needed, that is by decreasing the amount of the excess reactant. Foams, inert gas and CO2 are effective for smothering.

blocks.title: Checking the print
blocks.text: Sample 4.17 gives the NH3 mass as 1.81 g in the question and 18.1 g in the solution (18.1 g gives 1.06 mol), and multiplies the N2 moles by 17.0 instead of the molar mass of N2, 28.0, printing 9.0 g; with 28.0 the mass is 10.6 g.

blocks.prompt: Which mixture gives the most NH3 by N2 + 3H2 = 2NH3: (a) 1 mol N2 with 3 mol H2, (b) 2 mol N2 with 3 mol H2, (c) 1 mol N2 with 5 mol H2, (d) 3 mol N2 with 3 mol H2?
blocks.explanation: Find the limiting reactant in each. (a) exact ratio: 2 mol NH3. (b) H2 limits: 3 mol H2 gives 2 mol NH3. (c) N2 limits: 1 mol N2 gives 2 mol NH3. (d) H2 limits: 2 mol NH3. Every mixture gives the same 2 mol of product.

items: Three steps: moles of each reactant; product each could give by the equation; the one giving least is limiting. CuO limits in Sample 4.17 (0.38 mol N2); sulfate limits in Sample 4.18 (0.05 mol, 15.2 g PbSO4).
